purpose: Discovery register for potentially useful open industrial-maintenance knowledge and data. It is not an imported fault database.

sources.title: Open-FDD — HVAC fault detection and diagnostics
sources.version: NF app VERSION 5.0.20; PyPI package pyproject 4.5.11; latest GitHub release open-fdd-v4.5.11
sources.dataLicense: not separately verified for any benchmark, demo, or telemetry data
sources.licenseStatus: MIT verified for repository code; no blanket data license established
sources.contentsReviewed: Inspected README, MIT LICENSE, VERSION, pyproject, security docs, NF app README, SQL/Pandas cookbooks, fdd-catalog.json, SQLite rule pack and representative FDD/Lite tests. The catalog contains 77 SQL rules; the cookbook lists 71 pandas twins (six SQL-only); 60 RCx charts; 52/77 rules require run-proof. Missing run proof is SKIPPED, not PASS. The rule catalog contains no per-rule source/reference fields. SQL/Pandas rules use Haystack roles, SI units, confirm windows and parity checks.
sources.dataOrigin: Repository documentation references HVAC datasets and external building/plant sources; individual source datasets and their redistribution terms were not reviewed in this pass.
sources.potentialUse: Architecture and rule-evaluation reference for HVAC FDD; next review should inspect rule equations, units, input roles, source citations and benchmark provenance.
sources.reportedScope: HVAC fault detection and diagnostics platform; current README describes SQL/Pandas rule catalogue and analytics.
sources.accessStatus: README, LICENSE, VERSION, pyproject, security docs, rule cookbooks, 77-rule catalog, SQLite pack and representative tests inspected. No external benchmark data downloaded.
qualityNotes: Strong HVAC FDD engineering: 77 SQL rules, 71 pandas equivalents, SQL/Pandas parity tests, SI-unit contract and explicit run-proof gate.
52/77 rules require run proof; absent proof yields SKIPPED rather than a false PASS. Missing time gaps are treated as unknown.
The 77-rule catalog has no per-rule source references. Rule equations, thresholds and source rights need per-rule provenance review before any transfer into our fault knowledge base.
This is rule-based HVAC fault detection/retro-commissioning, not a general industrial causal root-cause engine or calibrated RUL model.
Full NF app requires Normal Framework and Python/SQL services; Lite is a dashboard edition and does not load FDD/RCX code. Neither is a direct Android/Worker dependency.
Security docs restrict deployment to trusted LAN/VPN/OT behind NF; public unauthenticated exposure is explicitly not production-hardened. NF provides auth; app does not write field devices.
GitHub API reported pushed_at 2026-11-18T18:54:55Z, about five minutes after this run's clock; master head commit 9526665 is dated 2026-11-16T23:08Z. Treat the push timestamp as clock-skewed.
Repository VERSION is 5.0.20 while pyproject/latest release is 4.5.11; these are separate app and Python package versions, not a single release number.
sources.dataLeakage: No benchmark leakage assessment performed; any future evaluation must split by site, asset and time, not random overlapping windows.
sources.dependencies: NF app uses Normal Framework edge services, SQL.js/PGlite, Haystack model/history, Python >=3.10 package, Pandas/SQL, Docker/NF deployment. Not suitable as a direct Android or Cloudflare Worker runtime dependency.
sources.androidWorkerCompatibility: Use architecture and safety patterns only. Any rule port must be individually reviewed for source, unit, equipment scope, operating proof, confirmation time and test parity; implement a small JS subset rather than importing Python/NF services.
sources.reuseConditions: MIT verified in LICENSE for repository code. External data and third-party source rights remain separate. No wholesale rule or dataset import until each rule's provenance and scope are documented.
sources.decision: architecture-and-rule-reference-only; selective rule adaptation after per-rule source-and-safety review

sources.contentsReviewed: Official UCI record confirms 2,205 multivariate 60-second cycles, 43,680 features, 17 sensor channels and four component condition labels (cooler, valve, pump internal leakage, accumulator). The dataset page explicitly states CC-BY-4.0.
sources.dataOrigin: ZeMA hydraulic test rig with cooler, valve, pump internal leakage and accumulator condition measurements.
qualityNotes: Labels describe laboratory test-rig component condition grades, not root-cause explanations or safe repair instructions.
Fault conditions are superimposed; labels are not independent causal fault diagnoses.
No raw-file validation or field generalization test was run.
sources.dataLeakage: Use operating-point/cycle-group splits; random row or window splitting can leak operating conditions and repeated-cycle patterns.
sources.androidWorkerCompatibility: Benchmark only; raw dataset is too large for the phone/Worker runtime.
sources.reuseConditions: CC BY 4.0 attribution; preserve dataset citation and source link; do not turn telemetry labels into maintenance facts.

sources.title: Hydraulic System Condition Monitoring — UCI 447 classifier study
sources.potentialUse: Methodology reference for reproducible classification, training-only model selection and evaluation of cooler, valve, pump and accumulator labels; not a causal diagnosis source.
sources.reportedScope: Study of UCI hydraulic dataset 447 with 2,205 cycles, 17 channels and four separate supervised classification targets; README reports 1,764 training and 441 final-test cycles.
sources.licenseStatus: No repository LICENSE file found; code reuse rights are not granted by the repository. Underlying UCI data is CC-BY-4.0 at its original source.
sources.accessStatus: README.md, PROJECT_GUIDE.md and requirements.txt inspected; no repository code or raw data copied.
sources.codeLicense: No repository LICENSE found; no code reuse permission verified.
sources.dataLicense: Underlying UCI dataset 447 is CC-BY-4.0; derived reports and code have no separate verified license.
sources.contentsReviewed: Reviewed the reported training-only CV protocol, 80/20 stratified per-target split, feature definitions, stable/transient subgroup notes and dependency requirements. No source code or raw UCI data was copied.
qualityNotes: The task is supervised component-state classification, not forecasting or causal root-cause diagnosis.
The per-target stratified cycle split may place adjacent or correlated cycles across train/test; grouped and chronological holdouts are needed before accepting generalization claims.
Reported accuracy and macro-F1 are dataset-specific metrics, not calibrated fault probabilities or field validation.
sources.androidWorkerCompatibility: Research reference only; Python/scikit-learn pipeline is not an Android/Worker runtime dependency.
sources.reuseConditions: Use the original UCI dataset under CC BY 4.0 with attribution if needed; do not copy this repository's code or derived artifacts without a license.

sources.title: Operating-state-aware monitoring — hydraulic and bearing research
sources.potentialUse: Reference for operating-state segmentation, grouped splits and measurement-family ablation on hydraulic data; not a repair knowledge base.
sources.reportedScope: Hydraulic case uses UCI 447; README reports 1,449 stable cycles divided into 144 contiguous condition blocks and compares pressure/flow, motor power, temperature and vibration feature families.
sources.licenseStatus: No repository LICENSE file found; code reuse rights are not granted. The original UCI data source is CC-BY-4.0; repository mirror rights are not independently verified.
sources.accessStatus: README.md and data/hydraulic/README.md inspected; raw mirror files and source code were not downloaded.
sources.codeLicense: No repository LICENSE found; no code reuse permission verified.
sources.dataLicense: Underlying UCI dataset 447 is CC-BY-4.0 at the original source; mirror copy and derived artifacts not separately licensed.
sources.contentsReviewed: Reviewed the README's operating-state split description, block counts, feature families and data/hydraulic/README.md source citation. Raw files were not downloaded or copied.
qualityNotes: Grouped splitting is a stronger leakage-control direction than random row splits, but the 144 blocks are not proven independent experimental runs.
The repository describes a descriptive research study and explicitly avoids claiming universal sensor optimality, causal leakage mechanism or production readiness.
Use UCI's original source and license rather than copying an unlicensed repository mirror.
sources.androidWorkerCompatibility: Methodology reference only; Python research code and raw multivariate time series are not runtime dependencies.
sources.reuseConditions: Do not reuse repository code or mirrored data without explicit rights. If using UCI data, obtain it from UCI under CC BY 4.0 and attribute the original authors.
